newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle surge to 10-month highs.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle surge to 10-month highs.

text.p: Active speculative fund buying and buy stops shot June CME live cattle up to 10-month highs with October and December setting new contract highs. All months of feeder cattle set new contract highs as fund buying added to short covering from firm cash ideas, traders said.

Live cattle finished with gains of 1.275 to 0.425 cents per lb with June up most at 66.100 cents, highest level since July 17, 1996. October posted a new contract high of 69.525 and December 71.200 cents.
Feeder cattle ended up 1.200 to 0.300 with August up 0.975 at 77.400 after setting a new high of 77.575 cents.

Live cattle started their rally on speculation cash markets may be firmer next week instead of easier as had been expected earlier this week. Cattle were pulled ahead at feedlots and a smaller showlist was projected for next week at possibly higher prices, traders said.
"There was some cash talk that we were going to be up to $70 (per cwt) next week," said Karl Skold, Director of Research for Frontier Risk Management.
However, Skold as well as many other analysts and traders attributed the bulk of the run up in futures to technicals.
"We had a technical breakout and it was heavily bought," Skold said.
Spreaders were also unwinding short June/long August spreads earlier. Those spreads had been put on ahead of fund rolling that started Wednesday, they said.

Rosenthal Collins notably bought on the start of the rally with R.J. O'Brien actively buying late while Cargill Investor Services sold. Cargill bought August along with Dean Witter, Fimat Futures USA and Shatkin. In options, commission houses sold 66 June calls and then bought the 65 straddle. They also sold August 68 and 69 puts late, pit sources said.

Feeder cattle futures also ran up on short covering and fund buying to post new contract highs. Futures started higher on short covering stimulated by expectations of stronger cash markets and a higher index next week, traders said.
Demand for heavier weight feeders to go on feed prompted support and offset higher corn futures, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.16 to $73.08 per cwt.

Rolling of long May contracts into August also subsided but Refco and E.D.&F. Man bought August and sold May early. Refco and Lind-Waldock bought May while Rosenthal Collins bought August. LFG sold May while locals sold August, pit sources said.
